title: Right-size vCenter CPU settings across a session token expiry
prompt:
Complete the root Go package `cpusweep` (module `vcf90-0048`, standard library only) as a focused VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 vSphere Automation API integration for vCenter. An operator right-sizes the CPU settings of a selected set of virtual machines. The session token that authenticates the sweep expires part way through it: the package must acquire a new one and carry on, replaying only the request that was interrupted and never repeating work it already committed.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection of `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0`, commit `85151f6b1bb58f13b6ac0304bfec53904bea085f`. It was derived from that OpenAPI document, not from a rendered documentation page and not from the 9.1 revision of the same path. The specification path, that commit, and every operationId are repeated in protected `docs/official_sources.json`. The only operationIds in scope are `Cis.Session_create`, `Vcenter.VM_list`, `Vcenter.Vm.Hardware.Cpu_get`, and `Vcenter.Vm.Hardware.Cpu_update`; do not contact any other vCenter route. The contract's server URL is `https://{host}/api`, so every wire target is the `/api` base path followed by the operation's specification path.

The public models, error types, validated construction, and the incomplete workflow and its helpers are in `client.go`. Preserve that public surface and implement these rules:

- `NewClient(Config)` treats `BaseURL` as an HTTP(S) origin and performs no traffic. Reject embedded credentials, query, fragment, a non-root path, a blank or ASCII-whitespace-bearing `Username` or `Password`, and `MaxReauth < 1`. A nil HTTP client means `http.DefaultClient`, a nil `OnReauth` callback is a no-op, and redirects are not followed. A `Client` holds no session state and is safe for concurrent use; each sweep owns its own session.
- `Sweep(ctx, SweepRequest)` rejects a nil or already-cancelled context locally. `Desired` must manage at least one `Vcenter.Vm.Hardware.Cpu.UpdateSpec` member. `Count` and `CoresPerSocket` must be positive, and when both are set `Count` must be a multiple of `CoresPerSocket`. Both filter slices carry `uniqueItems`, so entries must be nonblank, free of surrounding whitespace, and unique; `PowerStates` accepts only `POWERED_OFF`, `POWERED_ON`, and `SUSPENDED`. Reject invalid input before sending traffic.
- Log in with `Cis.Session_create` as exactly `POST /api/session`, authenticated with the contract's `basic_auth` scheme and carrying no query, body, or `Content-Type`. Accept exactly HTTP 201 `application/json` holding a JSON string; a blank or whitespace-bearing token is a `*ProtocolError`. Authenticate every other operation with the contract's `api_key_auth` header `vmware-api-session-id` and never send basic credentials there.
- Invoke `Vcenter.VM_list` as exactly `GET /api/vcenter/vm`. Both filters serialize `style: form` with `explode: true`, so send one repeated parameter per value in caller order, `names` before `power_states`. A nil or empty filter is unset: emit no parameter for it, and emit no dangling query delimiter when nothing is filtered. Accept exactly HTTP 200 `application/json` and require the contract-required nonblank `vm`, `name`, and `power_state` on every summary. Process the returned machines in server order.
- For each machine invoke `Vcenter.Vm.Hardware.Cpu_get` as exactly `GET /api/vcenter/vm/{vm}/hardware/cpu`. The `vm` parameter is an opaque string, so escape it as one path segment. Send no query or body, accept exactly HTTP 200 `application/json`, and require all four `Cpu.Info` members.
- Every `UpdateSpec` member is optional, so send only the members whose current value differs from `Desired`. Emit compact JSON in contract order: `count`, `cores_per_socket`, `hot_add_enabled`, `hot_remove_enabled`. A member that is unmanaged or already correct must be omitted entirely, never sent as a zero value or an explicit null. The specification permits `hot_add_enabled` and `hot_remove_enabled` to be modified only while the machine is powered off: when `power_state` is not `POWERED_OFF`, drop those members and record them in `Outcome.Deferred` instead. Record the members actually sent in `Outcome.Changed`. When nothing remains to send, make no `Vcenter.Vm.Hardware.Cpu_update` call at all and leave `Outcome.Updated` false.
- Otherwise invoke `Vcenter.Vm.Hardware.Cpu_update` as exactly `PATCH /api/vcenter/vm/{vm}/hardware/cpu` with `Content-Type: application/json` and that body, and accept exactly HTTP 204 with an empty body.
- When any `api_key_auth` operation answers HTTP 401, run `Cis.Session_create` again and replay the identical request exactly once with the new token: same method, target, query, and body bytes. Do not re-list the inventory, re-read a machine you already read, or re-apply an update you already committed. A 401 on the replay returns `*APIError` and never triggers a second refresh for that request, and a 401 from `Cis.Session_create` itself is never refreshed.
- `MaxReauth` bounds the refreshes one sweep may perform. Exceeding it returns `*ReauthLimitError` carrying the operationId that needed the refresh and the limit. `SweepResult.Reauths` counts completed refreshes.
- Invoke `OnReauth(ctx, "Cis.Session_create", refreshCount)` immediately before each refresh with a 1-based count, and never before the initial login. A callback error or context cancellation stops traffic immediately and is returned unwrapped.
- Return the partial `SweepResult` alongside any error: `Outcomes` holds every machine completed before the failure, in server order.
- Every request sends `Accept: application/json`. GETs send no `Content-Type`, body, transfer encoding, query beyond the declared filters, or dangling query delimiter. Enforce the declared success status and media type, and reject malformed, trailing, or oversized success JSON with `*ProtocolError`.
- Decode non-success JSON into `*APIError`, preserving operationId, status, `error_type`, the `default_message` of each `Vapi.Std.LocalizableMessage`, and the `Vapi.Std.Errors.Unauthenticated` `challenge`. Use `*TransportError` for transport failures and preserve cancellation through `errors.Is`. Error strings must not expose the password, a session token, the challenge, a decoded server message, the response body, or the underlying transport text.

The protected `internal/contractmock` fixture loads and pins exactly those four routes from `docs/contract.json`, listens only on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port, generates its credentials, session tokens, and machine identifiers at runtime, and exposes a race-safe request log plus the updates it actually committed. Its tokens expire after a configured number of authenticated requests, and it rejects hot-plug members sent to a machine that is not powered off. Protected table-driven tests drive the expiry to every position in the workflow and check provenance hashes, exact targets, escaped identifiers, query and header shape, body bytes and member sets, omission of unset optional members, verbatim replay, refresh budgets and pacing, local validation, structured errors, and redaction under `go test -race`. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.

Do not modify `go.mod`, `contract_test.go`, `.gitignore`, `docs/`, or `internal/contractmock/`; edit only `client.go`. Run `go test -race -count=1 -timeout 60s ./...`.
scenario: a vCenter CPU right-sizing sweep whose session token expires part way through and must be refreshed so the interrupted request is replayed without repeating committed work
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback fixture expires the token at every position in the workflow and the verifier rejects any request whose wire shape differs, including an optional UpdateSpec member sent empty rather than omitted
